item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.4
item.description:
A web address typed into the launcher opens in the browser.

Added

  • A web address typed into the launcher is offered to be opened in the browser: amazon.com, github.com/hinkolas/inky, localhost:3000, or one spelled out with https://. Return opens it, ⌘↵ copies it as a link, and ⌘N, or Create Quicklink under ⌘K, opens the editor for a new quicklink with the address filled in. Whatever ends in a top-level domain counts, so the name of a file such as main.rs is offered too, above the file itself. Settings → Browser switches it off.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.3
item.description:
What is typed into the launcher is no longer lost when it closes.

Added

  • The launcher opens again where it was left. A click elsewhere, or the hotkey pressed again, puts it away as it is: the search, the selected result, what was typed into arguments, a command that is open. Opened again within a minute, it shows what it did. Settings → General sets how long, from never to always. Escape and ⌘W still close it for good.
  • ↑ in the empty search brings back what was searched for before, newest first, with what was typed into a quicklink's arguments and the result that was selected. ↑ and ↓ then go through the earlier searches until something is typed; ⌃N and ⌃P move the selection meanwhile. A search is remembered when it is run, cleared with Escape, or closed with ⌘W, and the same search is listed once. Settings → General sets how many are kept, the last 100 unless chosen otherwise, and clears them.

Changed

  • Files that were found stay listed while the same search is looked up again, as when an application was installed meanwhile, instead of going and coming back.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.2
item.description:
Where the keyboard is in the launcher, which the first testers found unreliable.

Fixed

  • The launcher puts the keyboard into the field of the screen it shows and keeps it there, instead of leaving that to how soon macOS moves focus to a field that has just appeared. This covers opening the launcher right after closing it, opening the clipboard history, the quicklinks or another command with its hotkey, and renaming a pinned entry of the clipboard history.
  • Going back to a list, as from editing a quicklink or from what uninstalling an application would remove, puts the keyboard into its filter again. Before, typing did nothing until the filter was clicked.
  • In the quicklink editor, Tab goes from the link back to the name. Before, it left the keyboard with neither. Editing a quicklink puts the insertion point at the end of its link instead of selecting all of it.
  • Typing is never lost to a launcher that is open: should the keyboard be with no field at all, the first key puts it back where it belongs.
